models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign at Portorosa tonight; tomorrow is a soft, mostly windless day - watch Sunday's W'ly build.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the southern Tyrrhenian - winds are light and largely diurnal, swinging through most of the compass as sea breeze and drainage flow take over. Overnight the flow at Portorosa settles SSW-SSE at around 5 kt (ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg, 09 Oct 00Z, in consensus with AIFS 06Z and ICON-2i 00Z), with models disagreeing on strength at midnight across a 1.7 to 10.3 kt range. Through Saturday the pattern stays slack, 3 to 7 kt backing SW then W, before a genuine W to NW airstream fills in late Saturday night into Sunday - 10 to 14 kt mean with gusts in the 20s and seas building to 3 to 4 ft across the island group.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Portorosa Marina is the recommendation and the only option scored - enclosed, all-round shelter, so the choice does not matter tonight. The berth forecast is 4.7 kt SSE gusting 13.4 kt with 0.9 ft WNW swell outside (ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg, 09 Oct 00Z); by 06:00 wind nudges to around 7 kt with gusts to 17.5 kt and 1.4 ft wave outside the breakwater. Nothing here would move the fleet - normal marina lines and springs are enough.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Saturday looks slack: Portorosa 2.6 kt W gusting 11.3 kt at midday, 4.6 kt SW gusting 17.1 kt by evening, wave around 1.2 to 1.3 ft (ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg, 09 Oct 00Z). The payload carries no leg forecast for tomorrow and the berth list keeps the fleet at Portorosa Marina on 10 Oct, so I have no departure window to give you - if you intend to move, treat the morning as a motoring day and ask for a fresh window. The one caveat is the 06:00 period, when ICON-2i and MFWAM show interval-maximum gusts of 40.6 kt at Lipari, 43.3 kt at Stromboli and 40.4 kt at Filicudi against means of 7 to 12 kt, which reads as isolated convection rather than gradient wind.

passage_notes.note: Today's leg, verdict go, recommended departure 06:00 with deterioration after 12:00. Best windows were 06:00-10:00 (3.4 kt SSW, 0.7 ft, close hauled) and 08:00-12:00 (4.6 kt E, 0.6 ft); the 12:00 slot was flagged no-go on thunderstorms in the window. Motoring conditions throughout.

passage_notes.leg: Next leg (not yet in the payload)
passage_notes.note: No forecast leg beyond Salina to Portorosa is provided, and the berth list keeps the fleet at Portorosa on 10 Oct. I cannot give a routing or departure window for a leg I do not have.

cautions: Isolated thunderstorms were already in today's midday window; the 06:00 Saturday interval-maximum gusts of 40.6 kt (Lipari), 43.3 kt (Stromboli) and 40.4 kt (Filicudi) against 7-12 kt means suggest the convective risk has not fully cleared.

Sunday 11 Oct brings the real change: W to NW 10-15 kt with a 3.9-23.9 kt model spread at Filicudi at midnight, gusts to 31.7 kt, and total wave to 3.5-3.7 ft at Salina, Lipari and Filicudi. Plan Saturday with that in mind.
Direction, not strength, is the weak point in light air - forecast stability over 12-24 h shows a mean direction shift of 75 deg between runs. Do not plan a sail angle on tonight's numbers.
MFWAM is the oldest input here at 24.1 h (08 Oct 12Z); the sea-state figures deserve a cross-check against ECMWF WAM before relying on them.
briefing.confidence_note: The models agree that it stays light - mean run-to-run wind shift is only 1.7 kt at 12-24 h - but they disagree on overnight strength at Portorosa across 1.7 to 10.3 kt and the direction field is unstable at 75 deg mean shift, which is typical of a slack pattern.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
